title: Choose the visual world
question: The roll assigned the Dakar Route Map. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: Dakar Route Map
options.lineage: the printed road maps riders carried across the Sahara on the 1990s Paris–Dakar
options.thesis: The strip-down as a route: every assembly is a stage on the road from whole machine to bare frame.
options.viewport: The whole RD07 alone and large on a pale map sheet; a red route line leaves its rear wheel and runs down into the scroll, stage 01 marked in the margin.
options.risk: The route metaphor turns decorative if a stage ever fails to name its part plainly.

raised.raise: Route red is owned outright: it floods each stage band edge to edge instead of appearing as scattered accents.
Every part carries its strip-down order number on the drawing itself, like lamps numbered on a fabrication elevation.
Each explanation is pinned to an exact frame of the strip-down, cited like a stage kilometre, so text and image never drift.
The map prints in four true spot inks that overprint where they cross; no soft gradients anywhere.
The Tripmaster counts the route: a mechanical odometer rolls the stage distance as each assembly comes off.

options.label: Rally Roadbook
options.lineage: the paper roadbook rolls Dakar riders scroll through while riding
options.thesis: The page scrolls like a rally roadbook: each assembly is a numbered box with its tulip diagram, distance and note.
options.viewport: The whole RD07 centred above the first roadbook box: 0.00 km, depart, with the roll continuing below the fold.
options.risk: Tulip notation is niche; visitors who never rode a rally need every box to read as a plain step.

options.label: Crank Automaton
options.thesis: Scroll is the crank: each assembly opens into its own linkage, one crimson fold reserved for the part in motion.
options.viewport: The RD07 as a cut-paper figure on kraft board, a crank line ruling the base, its shadow cast on the wall behind.
options.case: Holds product clarity (every linkage opens in order) but loses identification: riders do not know paper automata.
options.risk: Paper can make a 234 kg machine read as a toy.

options.label: Nixie Counter
options.thesis: Every specification as a lit tube bank.
options.viewport: Spec banks glowing beside the bike.
options.case: Loses both axes: specs gain drama but the build order disappears, and riders do not read lab counters.
options.risk: Drifts toward the glowing tech look.
options.kept: The Tripmaster rolls stage distance as a mechanical count.

options.label: Hand-processed 16mm
options.thesis: The strip-down as a scratched film strip.
options.viewport: A film strip with the bike in its frames.
options.case: Loses both axes: the film surface competes with the bike and says nothing about how it is built.
options.risk: Grain and leaks read as a filter.
options.kept: Text is pinned to exact frames.

options.label: Single-hue program
options.viewport: The bike on a flood of red.
options.case: Loses both axes: reads as a brand campaign, the official-ad look you ruled out.
options.kept: One colour owns its fields outright.

options.label: Desert sign elevation
options.lineage: desert strip neon sign working drawings
options.thesis: Parts as numbered lamp banks on a sign elevation.
options.viewport: A dimensioned elevation of the bike.
options.case: Loses both axes: American roadside, not Saharan rally.
options.kept: Order numbers live on the drawing itself.

options.label: Risograph system
options.case: Loses both axes: zine energy with no link to rallying or mechanics.
options.risk: Playful where the machine is serious.
options.kept: True spot inks that overprint, no gradients.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: The dark studio product page, executed impeccably.
canonCard.viewport: The RD07 floating on black under a soft key light, with its name and one spec line beneath.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from every launch page, and the closest to the official-ad feel you ruled out.
